column1: contemptuous§Her contemptuous dismissal of the question told the room more about her position than any answer would have.§她**轻蔑地**打发掉这个问题，比任何回答都更清楚地暴露了她的立场。§con-（加强）+ temn（轻视）
contend§Three teams contended for a grant that, when finally awarded, turned out to cover about half the work proposed.§三支团队**争夺**一笔经费，而它最终发下来时只够覆盖计划中约一半的工作。§con-（一起）+ tend（伸展，同 tension 张力）→ 互相较劲
contentious§The most contentious clause is also the shortest: nine words about who owns the data once the study ends.§最**有争议的**条款也是最短的——九个词，说明研究结束后数据归谁。§
contiguous§The two properties are contiguous, which is why a fence built six inches wrong has occupied two lawyers for a year.§这两处地产**紧邻**，所以一道偏了六英寸的围栏让两名律师忙了一年。§con-（一起）+ tig（接触，同 contact 接触）
contingency§No contingency covered a two-week power failure, because nobody drafting the plan believed one could happen.§没有任何**应急预案**涵盖为期两周的断电，因为起草方案的人都不信这会发生。§con-（一起）+ ting（接触，同 contact 接触）→ 碰巧发生
continual§The continual interruptions made the work take three times as long as the same task done at home.§**接连不断的**打断让这份工作耗时是在家做同样任务的三倍。§
continuously§The sensor has run continuously since 1974, and its record is the longest unbroken series anyone has for this coast.§这台传感器自 1974 年起**不间断地**运行，其记录是这段海岸现有最长的连续序列。§
contour§The contour of the valley floor decides everything: water collects in three places, and all three flooded that April.§谷底的**地形起伏**决定了一切——水汇聚在三处，那年四月三处全淹了。§con-（一起）+ tour（转，同 tour 巡回）→ 描一圈边线
contract§The contract runs eleven pages, and the clause that ended the partnership sits in the middle of page nine.§这份**合同**长十一页，终结这段合伙关系的条款就在第九页中间。§con-（一起）+ tract（拉，同 attract 吸引）→ 拉到一起立约
contrive§She contrived to see the file by volunteering for the one shift nobody else wanted.§她**设法**看到了那份文件——办法是主动去上那个没人愿意上的班。§
controversy§The controversy outlived the paper that caused it, and most people arguing now have read only the summaries.§这场**争论**比引发它的论文活得更久，如今争论的人多数只读过摘要。§contro（相对）+ vers（转，同 reverse 倒转）→ 两边对着转
conundrum§The conundrum is practical, not philosophical: the only road out floods exactly when the town most needs to evacuate.§这个**难题**是现实的而非哲学的——唯一的出城路恰在小镇最需要撤离时被淹。§

convention§Convention, not law, keeps the two offices separate, and conventions hold only while everyone agrees to hold them.§让这两个部门分立的是**惯例**而非法律，而惯例只在人人都愿遵守时才成立。§con-（一起）+ ven（来，同 event 事件）→ 大家聚过来的老规矩
convergence§The convergence of the two lines of evidence was the turning point: neither alone would have persuaded anyone.§两条证据线的**汇聚**是转折点——单靠任何一条都说服不了人。§con-（一起）+ verg（倾斜，同 verge 边缘）→ 斜向同一点
convergent§Bats and birds are a convergent pair: they arrived at flight separately, from very different bones.§蝙蝠和鸟是一对**趋同**演化的例子——它们各自从很不同的骨骼演化出飞行。§
convict§The jury convicted him on the strength of one witness, and that witness recanted eleven years later.§陪审团凭一名证人的证词**判他有罪**，那名证人十一年后翻了供。§con-（完全）+ vict（战胜，同 victory 胜利）→ 在法庭上被彻底击败
conviction§Her conviction that the data were wrong kept her checking for two years, and in the end the data were wrong.§她**坚信**数据有误，为此核查了两年，最后数据确实错了。§

convivial§The dinner was convivial until someone mentioned the will, and the last hour was conducted almost entirely in silence.§这顿晚餐**其乐融融**，直到有人提起遗嘱，最后一小时几乎全程沉默。§con-（一起）+ viv（生活，同 survive 幸存）→ 凑一块儿热闹地过
convolute§The regulations convolute a simple duty into eleven steps, and three of the steps refer to each other.§这些规定把一项简单的义务**盘绕**成十一个步骤，其中三步还互相指来指去。§con-（一起）+ volut（卷，同 revolve 旋转）
cooperation§Cooperation between the two agencies exists on the organizational chart and almost nowhere else.§两家机构之间的**合作**存在于组织结构图上，别处几乎见不到。§
cooperative§The most cooperative witness was also the least useful, since he agreed with whatever the last question implied.§最**配合的**证人同时也是最没用的——上一个问题暗示什么，他就同意什么。§
copious§She took copious notes and never reread them, which she now describes as the most expensive habit of her twenties.§她记了**大量**笔记，却从不重读，如今她称之为二十几岁时最昂贵的习惯。§copi（丰富，同 copy 复本／abundance）
cordial§Relations remained cordial in public and were finished in private, and the joint statement fooled nobody who worked there.§关系在公开场合保持**热诚**，私下里已经结束，联合声明骗不了任何在那儿工作的人。§cord（心，同 cordial 由衷的）
corollary§A useful corollary follows: if the cost falls by half, the same budget reaches twice as many households.§由此得出一条有用的**推论**——若成本减半，同样的预算就能覆盖两倍的家庭。§co-（一起）+ roll ← corolla（花冠／小赏金）→ 顺带得出的
corpulence§His corpulence became a political cartoonist's shorthand, and the actual policies he passed are now largely forgotten.§他的**肥胖**成了政治漫画家的速记符号，而他实际推行的政策如今大多被遗忘。§corpor（身体，同 corporation 法人团体）
corrective§The corrective was simple and late: a second signature on every order, introduced four months after the loss.§**纠正措施**简单而迟到——每份订单加一个签名，在损失发生四个月后才推行。§cor-（加强）+ rect（正，同 correct 正确的）
correlation§The correlation is strong and the causation is unknown, which has not stopped anyone from writing headlines about it.§**相关性**很强而因果关系未知，这并未阻止任何人为此写标题。§cor-（一起）+ relat（关联，同 relate 相关）

corrosive§Her sarcasm was corrosive over time: nobody objected to any single remark, and after a year nobody spoke freely.§她的讥讽日久便有**腐蚀性**——没人反对某一句话，一年后却没人再敢畅所欲言。§cor-（加强）+ ros（啃，同 rodent 啮齿动物）→ 一点点啃掉
cosmetic§The changes were cosmetic: a new name, a new logo, and the same three people making the same decisions.§这些改变只是**表面功夫**——新名字、新标志，还是那三个人做着同样的决定。§

cosmopolitan§The port was cosmopolitan four centuries before the word existed: eleven languages were spoken on one street.§这座港口在这个词出现前四百年就已**四海杂处**——一条街上说着十一种语言。§cosmo（世界，同 cosmos 宇宙）+ polit（城市，同 politics 政治）
counteract§Two extra crews counteracted the delay, and the project finished within a week of its original date.§两支额外的施工队**抵消**了延误，项目在原定日期一周内完工。§counter（反）+ act（作用）
counterfeit§The counterfeit was good enough to pass three banks and failed only because the serial numbers repeated.§这张**伪钞**做得足以骗过三家银行，唯一败露之处是编号重复。§counter（相对）+ feit ← fac（做，同 factory 工厂）→ 照着做一个假的
counterfeiter§The counterfeiter was an engraver by trade, and the plates he cut are now in a museum two miles from the courthouse.§这名**伪造者**本行是雕版师，他刻的印版如今陈列在离法院两英里的博物馆里。§
counterproductive§The penalty proved counterproductive: reporting fell by half, and the underlying problem grew for another three years.§这项处罚被证明**适得其反**——上报量减半，底下的问题又长了三年。§
courteous§He remained courteous through an hour of hostile questioning, which the transcript conveys and the recording does not.§整整一小时的敌意质询中他始终**彬彬有礼**，这一点文字记录传达得出，录音则不然。§court（宫廷）→ 有宫廷礼数的
covert§The covert program ran for eleven years on a budget line labelled "facilities maintenance."§这项**秘密**计划靠一条名为「设施维护」的预算线运行了十一年。§cover（遮盖）→ 盖起来的
covet§He coveted the corner office for six years and found, within a month of getting it, that he missed the noise.§他**觊觎**那间角落办公室六年，得到后不到一个月就发现自己怀念从前的嘈杂。§
cowardice§What looked like cowardice was calculation: he knew the charge would collapse and wanted someone else to say so first.§看着像**怯懦**的其实是算计——他知道指控会垮，只想让别人先说出来。§
cowardly§The most cowardly sentence in the report is the one that says mistakes "were made" and names nobody.§报告里最**怯懦的**一句，是那句说「出现了失误」却不点任何人名字的话。§
creativity§Creativity here is mostly editing: the first draft is nobody's best work, and the fourth usually is.§这里的**创造力**多半是编辑——初稿从来不是谁的最好水平，第四稿通常才是。§creat（造，同 create 创造）
credence§The rumour gained credence because three respectable people repeated it, none of whom had checked it.§这个传闻获得了**采信**，因为三位体面人重复了它，而他们谁也没核实过。§cred（相信，同 credit 信用）
credibility§The station lost its credibility in one broadcast and spent nine years trying to earn it back.§这家电台一次播出就丢掉了**公信力**，随后花了九年试图挣回来。§
credo§His credo fits on one line: measure first, argue second, and never trust a number you did not collect.§他的**信条**一行就写得下——先测量，再争论，绝不相信不是自己收的数字。§cred（相信）
credulity§The scheme survived on public credulity: it promised a return no honest business has ever produced.§这个骗局靠公众的**轻信**存活——它许诺的回报是任何正当生意从未做到过的。§cred（相信）+ -ulity（易于）
crisis§The crisis was over in nine days, and the changes it forced through had been blocked for the previous eleven years.§这场**危机**九天就结束，而它逼成的那些改革在此前十一年一直被搁置。§
critic§The critic who destroyed the first book praised the second, and never mentioned that they were by the same author.§毁掉第一本书的那位**批评家**称赞了第二本，却从未提及两本出自同一作者。§crit（判断，同 criterion 标准）
critical§The next four hours are critical: after that the concrete sets, and every mistake becomes permanent.§接下来四小时**至关重要**——之后混凝土凝固，任何错误都成了永久的。§
criticism§The criticism was fair and the timing was not: it arrived the morning the exhibition opened.§这番**批评**很公允，时机则不然——它出现在展览开幕的当天早上。§
crucial§One crucial detail was left out of every briefing: the pump had failed the same test twice before.§一个**关键**细节在每次简报中都被略去——那台泵此前已两次未通过同一项测试。§cruc（十字，同 crucifix 十字架）→ 岔路口的抉择
crude§The estimate is crude but honest: nobody has counted, and the range it gives is wide enough to say so.§这个估算**粗略**却诚实——没人清点过，它给出的区间宽到足以说明这一点。§crud（生的，同 crudité 生鲜蔬菜）
cryptic§His note was cryptic enough that the family spent a decade arguing about what he had meant by "the blue file."§他的字条**隐晦**到让家人为「那个蓝色文件夹」的含义争论了十年。§crypt（隐藏，同 crypt 地下墓室）
crystal§Her account was crystal clear where the official one was vague, which is why the committee believed her.§官方说法含糊之处她的陈述却**清澈**分明，这正是委员会相信她的原因。§
culpable§The report finds the supervisor culpable and the system blameless, which reverses what the evidence actually shows.§报告认定主管**有过失**而系统无咎，这与证据实际显示的恰好相反。§culp（过错）
cultivate§He cultivated the relationship for four years before asking for anything, which is why the answer was yes.§他**经营**这段关系四年才开口求助，所以得到的答复是肯定的。§cult（耕种，同 agriculture 农业）
cumulative§The cumulative effect is what matters: no single night of poor sleep hurts much, and ninety of them do.§起作用的是**累积**效应——单独一晚睡不好无甚大碍，九十晚就有了。§cumul（堆积，同 accumulate 积累）
cunning§The design is cunning rather than complex: one moving part does the work of the nine it replaced.§这个设计**精巧**而非复杂——一个活动部件干了它所取代的九个部件的活。§
curable§The disease is curable and the cure is unaffordable, which makes the statistics look like a medical problem.§这种病**可治愈**，而治疗费负担不起，这让统计数据看上去像个医学问题。§cur（照料，同 cure 治愈）
curative§The curative effect appeared in the trial and vanished in the field, and it took six years to work out why.§**治疗**效果在试验中出现，到实际应用中消失，弄清原因花了六年。§
curiosity§Her curiosity was the whole method: she asked the caretaker a question that nine researchers had never thought to ask.§她的**好奇心**就是全部方法——她问了看门人一个九位研究者从没想到要问的问题。§cur（照料／关心）→ 上心去打听
cursory§A cursory glance at the accounts would have caught it, and the accounts went unopened for two years.§**草草**看一眼账目就能发现，而那些账目两年没人翻开过。§curs（跑，同 current 水流）→ 跑着扫一眼
curtail§The city curtailed bus service in January, and by June ridership had fallen far below what the cuts had assumed.§这座城市一月**削减**了公交服务，到六月客流已远低于削减方案的假设。§curt（短，同 curt 简短的）
customization§Customization was the selling point and became the trap: no two installations behave the same way.§**定制化**是卖点，后来成了陷阱——没有两套安装的表现是一样的。§
cynical§He is cynical about announcements and generous with people, which turns out to be a workable combination.§他对各种公告**愤世嫉俗**，对人却慷慨，事实证明这是一种可行的组合。§
cynicism§Cynicism cost the campaign more than opposition did: volunteers did not argue, they simply stopped coming.§**犬儒心态**给这场运动造成的损失超过反对派——志愿者不争辩，只是不再来了。§
dalliance§His dalliance with the theatre lasted two seasons and produced one play nobody has staged since.§他与戏剧的**逢场作戏**持续了两季，留下一部此后无人上演的剧本。§
